title: Absence of nontrivial local conserved quantities in a class of $U(1)$-symmetric spin-1 chains
abstract: We prove the absence of nontrivial local conserved quantities in a class of $U(1)$-symmetric spin-$1$ chains with nearest-neighbor interactions in which some of the quadrupolar couplings vanish, a class that is not covered by previous studies. Applying the technique of Shiraishi to these systems, we show that, for every model in this class on a periodic chain of $N$ sites, there is no $k$-local conserved quantity for any $3\le k\le N/2$. In particular, for a frustration-free spin-$1$ chain that exhibits spontaneous $U(1)$ symmetry breaking at zero temperature in one spatial dimension, we prove that every local conserved quantity with support up to half of the system size is a linear combination of the identity, the total magnetization $S^z$, and the Hamiltonian itself. This rigorously establishes that, unlike the Heisenberg ferromagnet, the model admits no local order parameter commuting with the Hamiltonian, so that its continuous symmetry breaking is enabled by the frustration-free structure rather than by a conserved order parameter. We also prove the absence of $k$-local conserved quantities for $3\le k\le N/2$ in the periodic Motzkin chain, a frustration-free spin-$1$ chain closely related to the original Motzkin chain, for which spontaneous $U(1)$ symmetry breaking at zero temperature has also been reported.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that a specific class of U(1)-symmetric spin-1 chains lacks nontrivial local conserved quantities. By applying advanced commutator techniques, the authors show that the continuous symmetry breaking observed in these models is structural (due to frustration-free nature) rather than being protected by a conserved order parameter. This provides deep insight into the underlying dynamics and integrability of these quantum spin systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously prove the absence of nontrivial local conserved quantities in a specific, previously unstudied class of U(1)-symmetric spin-1 chains.
main_result: It establishes that for these models, any local conserved quantity with support up to half the system size must be a simple linear combination of the identity, the total magnetization, and the Hamiltonian itself.
method: The authors employ Shiraishi's technique, analyzing the commutator $[Q, H]$ for potential conserved charges $Q$ and solving the resulting linear system of equations.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1 chain on a periodic lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions, characterized by dipolar and quadrupolar couplings. The focus is on models where certain quadrupolar couplings vanish, including the frustration-free Motzkin chain.
key_observables: Local conserved quantities ($Q$), the total magnetization ($S_z$), and the Hamiltonian ($H$).
important_parameters: The size of the system ($N$) and the range of the conserved quantity support ($3 \le k \le N/2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending previous techniques to handle vanishing quadrupolar couplings, which was a gap in prior literature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the nonexistence of conserved quantities by first examining 2-local, then 3-local, and finally ruling out higher-order local charges using commutator analysis.
why_interesting: Proving the absence of local conserved quantities is a powerful tool for demonstrating non-integrability in quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and dynamics in condensed matter models.
